title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + ROPE/rotary fused ops + KV-batching scheduling optimizations
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: upgrade our attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 and roll in fused ROPE/rotary operations to reduce kernel launches and memory traffic, and tune KV-batching scheduling to reduce tail latency under mixed workloads. This PR consolidates kernel changes, scheduler hooks, and tests required to safely roll out the new kernels across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add FlashAttentionV2 kernels and build integration (third_party/flashattn v2 integration).
- Implement fused ROPE and rotary operator variants to avoid separate rotary kernels and reduce memory copies.
- Introduce scheduling hints for continuous batching and KV-cache-aware slotting to improve throughput/latency under mixed seq-length workloads.
- Add runtime feature-flagging and GPU capability fallback (SM70+ for v2 kernels, fallback to v1 for older cards).
- Update unit/integration tests and add perf benchmarks covering short (1-64), medium (65-512), and long (512-2048) sequences.
- Add telemetry and perf traces to help canary the rollout.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests
- [x] End-to-end perf benchmarks (internal harness)
- [x] Scheduler integration and smoke tests
- [x] Fallback behavior for unsupported GPUs
- [x] Docs/perf notes
- [x] Linear tickets linked

Benchmarks: (microbenchmarks on p4d with FP16, batch size 8 unless noted)
- 2k seq, 32k hidden: ~28% throughput improvement vs previous kernels
- 512 seq (chat-like): ~18% throughput improvement + 12% lower p95 latency in mixed workloads with tuned KV-batching scheduling
- 64 seq: ~15% improvement; important win is reduced CPU overhead and fewer kernel launches when ROPE/rotary is fused

Compatibility & safety:
- Feature-flag gate: runtime config: attention.kernels.use_flashattn_v2 (defaults to true for new clusters, false for older regions until canary)
- Fallback path implemented for SM<70 or when JIT compile fails at runtime (falls back to stable v1 kernels)
- Added extensive regression tests and a perf-gated CI job that must pass on a target GPU CI matrix before merge

Related: Linear ENG-1421 (attention perf lift), ENG-2173 (rollout plan), RFC:internal/attn-kernels/2025

Notes for reviewers: The kernel code changes are in cuda files under src/runtime/attention; most logic is isolated behind a new factory interface so we can A/B different kernels at runtime. Scheduler changes are limited to adding a KV-batching hint and a new scoring function for continuous batching; existing policies remain unchanged unless the new hint is enabled.

Merging: squash merge after perf CI passed and approvals. See CI history below for intermittent perf reruns; final state is green.
